classification.difficultyReason: Read supplied graphs to distinguish breaks and holes from connected curves and corners.

content.prompt: For these functions, identify the $x$ value(s) where the graph has a discontinuity, or state that the function is continuous.

spec.description: Two reciprocal-shaped branches with continuation arrows; unnumbered coordinate axes.
spec.mathematics: Separate branches in quadrants I and III approach both axes. No value is assigned at x=0.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph supplied to students; answer omitted.

answer.worked: The graph has a break at $x=0$, where the branches approach the vertical axis. Therefore the discontinuity is at $x=0$.

spec.description: Rising straight line with an open point above x₁; arrows at both ends and no numerical ticks.
spec.mathematics: The sole missing point on an otherwise connected straight line occurs at x=x₁.
spec.answerVisibility: Open point and x₁ label are supplied; answer omitted.

answer.worked: The open circle shows a hole at $x=x_1$. Therefore the function is discontinuous there.

spec.description: Unbroken U-shaped qualitative graph with a broad shallow minimum below the horizontal axis and left of the vertical axis.
spec.mathematics: Both ends rise, with two x-axis crossings and no holes, jumps or asymptotes.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph supplied to students; answer omitted.

answer.worked: The curve is unbroken, with no holes or jumps. Therefore the function is continuous.

spec.description: Connected curve with a sharp finite peak on the positive y-axis and outward arrows on the lower tails.
spec.mathematics: The two sides meet at a finite peak. The y-axis is not a vertical asymptote.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph supplied to students; answer omitted.

answer.worked: The two sides meet at the sharp peak without a break. A sharp peak does not prevent continuity, so the function is continuous.

spec.description: Dashed asymptote left of the y-axis at x₁; the right branch joins a rising ray at a connected corner above x₂.
spec.mathematics: There is an infinite break at x₁. The corner at x₂ is connected and is not a discontinuity.
spec.answerVisibility: Asymptote, corner and labels are supplied; answer omitted.

answer.worked: The vertical asymptote gives a discontinuity at $x=x_1$. At $x=x_2$, the pieces join without a break, so the corner is continuous.

spec.description: Increasing concave-down curve from a negative x-axis endpoint, with an open point and vertical dashed guide above b.
spec.mathematics: A single hole occurs at x=b; the curve continues to the right.
spec.answerVisibility: Open point and b guide are supplied; answer omitted.

answer.worked: The open circle shows a hole at $x=b$. Therefore the function is discontinuous there.
